summary: fastapii ships base64-obfuscated setup.py dropper that fetches and executes a Linux binary at install time
details: The pypi package fastapii 0.2.0 is a typosquat of fastapi whose setup.py registers a custom install command class (LinuxInstall) that, on pip install, decodes a base64-encoded Python payload and executes it via exec(compile(...)). The decoded hook, on Linux, downloads an opaque binary from an unrelated personal GitHub repository (github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW, release v1.3A/something) to /tmp/something, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached with stdout/stderr suppressed. The advertised package purpose is generic HTTP client utilities and the shipped module (djangoo) only exports a trivial hello function, so the install-time binary fetch has no legitimate build or runtime purpose. Installing the package executes attacker-controlled code on the host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
